join.title: Sing with us
join.intro: Do you love to sing and to serve God through music? Chorale Christus Regnat welcomes new members who want to praise God through liturgical and gospel music.

steps.title: Come to a rehearsal
steps.text: Visit us on a Tuesday or Friday evening at Ste Famille (JOC) and tell us you would like to join the choir.

steps.title: Choose your section
steps.text: Most people who join already sing, so you start in the section you know: soprano, alto, tenor or bass. You rehearse as a new member while the choir follows your attendance.

steps.title: Evaluation
steps.text: The technical team evaluates you and may move you to a section that suits you better. If you are not ready yet, you keep rehearsing and are evaluated again later.

steps.title: Become a full member
steps.text: After a successful evaluation, you are a full member: you take part in the General Assembly and pay the monthly contribution.

about.title: Singing to the glory of God since 2006
about.intro: Chorale Christus Regnat is a Catholic choir at Regina Pacis Parish in Remera, Kigali. We serve the liturgy with music that unites modern liturgical song, Gregorian chant and Rwandan traditional melodies.
story: The choir was born in 2006 at Centre Christus in Remera, started by Christians who wanted beautiful music at Mass. Parents and children sang side by side, and trained musicians soon joined them.

Today the choir counts more than 100 members of all ages. It sings at Mass at Regina Pacis Parish and in other churches of Kigali, and its annual concert, iBweranganzo, brings faith, music and many talents together.
music: We sing in Kinyarwanda, French, Latin, English and other languages, and we have recorded several albums.
Among our best-known songs are “Mama Shenge”, recorded with Yverry and Andy Bumuntu, and “Igipimo cy'Urukundo” by Cyprien Rugamba.
about.charityText: Faith also shows in what we do. The choir visits the sick, supports orphans and widows, pays health insurance (mutuelle de santé) for people who cannot afford it, and supports Dusangire Lunch, which gives school lunches to children.
